name: Arundo
look_here_first: GIANT REED: begin with robust jointed canes and broad clasping leaves; inspect the actual leaf collar and mature flowering plume in the licensed macro panels. For look-alike Phragmites, confirm glabrous Arundo spikelet RACHILLA versus long silky Phragmites rachilla hairs on a magnified ripe spikelet; the Arundo ligule itself CAN have a ciliate fringe. No removal or exact Phragmites lineage ID from plume size alone.

project_scope.note: First-pass source-pool learner anchors; unresolved range and comparison labels retained.

genus_diagnostics.habit: Dense stands of tall cane-like stems; selected photograph shows a stand in Maui, not a Texas locality.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Broad flat grass blades on conspicuous culms; sheath and ligule require close photographs.
genus_diagnostics.inflorescence: Large terminal panicle; panicle architecture and spikelet detail remain photo gaps.
genus_diagnostics.lookalike_separators: ARUNDO vs PHRAGMITES: Both make tall jointed riparian canes and feathery heads. Arundo usually has broad clasping leaf bases, a robust cane and a more upright branching panicle; common reed often has a more drooping plume. A definitive flowering check is WHERE HAIRS GROW: Arundo has a glabrous RACHILLA (axis between florets) but silky hairs on the basal lemma/callus; Phragmites has LONG SILKY RACHILLA HAIRS and usually glabrous lemmas. Their ligules can BOTH be fringed — a 'hairless Arundo ligule' is NOT a dependable rule. Do not call a Phragmites stand introduced/invasive without independent lineage evidence.

study_strategy.warning: Two physically archived Arundo images plus two externally hosted source-verified CC BY 2.0 review photos. Five gross-feature arrows only. Spikelet cross-section, same-scale ligule and rhizomes missing. Native Hays ranges untouched.
teaching_order: Actual ciliate ligule and clasping leaf base with safe arrows
Ripe spikelet with scaled Arundo rachilla versus Phragmites hairy rachilla
Phragmites native/introduction lineage separate from species ID

visual_comparison.title: ARUNDO — giant reed actual collar and seedhead
visual_comparison.subtitle: 2 originally archived physical photos + 2 newly verified CC BY 2.0 external source images with 5 accurately targeted gross-feature arrows. Phragmites microscopic hair-placement lesson remains awaiting matched dissection.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: ARUNDO: broad clasping cane leaves + upright panicle; RACHILLA HAIRLESS, HAIRY LEMMA BASE. PHRAGMITES: long RACHILLA hairs. BOTH may have fringed ligules; lineage ID is separate.

items.label: GIANT REED — real leaf collar, ciliate membranous ligule and clasping blade base
items.image_role: Exact source-identified Arundo macro from Australia: blade/sheath junction with visibly fringed membranous ligule and leaf-base lobes. A contrasting Phragmites collar is still needed at matched scale.
items.caption: This is the actual junction of blade and sheath. The pale collar has rounded clasping lobes; a whitish CILIATE fringe extends from the membranous ligule inside. Do NOT teach that Arundo has a hairless ligule; some comparative literature describes the leaf collar differently. Use leaf-base shape as a supporting clue, then confirm spikelet anatomy.
items.why_it_matters: Shows exactly where crews must inspect the ligule and wide clasping leaf base, and prevents a false hairless-Arundo shortcut. Photographed in Australia, not a Texas voucher.
items.creator: Harry Rose (Macleay Grass Man)
items.modification_note: Unaltered Commons photograph; educational arrows are separate browser overlays, not changes to source pixels.
items.photo_status: Source image inspected at 960×720 on 2026-10-21; real hairs and clasping collar visible. External, licensed provisional public-review panel; no archived local JPEG or mm ruler; PROVISIONAL — USER PHOTO REVIEW PENDING.

items.label: GIANT REED — actual tall upright branching flowering panicle
items.image_role: Actual source-determined photographed full flowering head from Australia; sees whole panicle branching, not individual florets or glumes.
items.caption: A complete flowering plume shows many slender side branches spreading off a central axis, with the overall panicle held upright. Panicle posture varies, so never separate giant reed from common reed by plume silhouette alone. Floret rachilla and lemma hairs cannot be seen at this magnification.
items.why_it_matters: Fills a true panicle view absent from the original habitat stand photographs; gives a reliable target for the first pass before dissecting florets.

part_examples.why_it_matters: Start with cane-like jointed culms from thick rhizomes, broad flat leaves, and the large terminal panicle. Inspect the ligule and mature spikelets to separate it from Phragmites; height alone is not a reliable key.
